locationId: CHANGE: exact locationId from story.json locations[]
narrativeBeat: place identity lock — the visual definition every page set here must match
primaryRequest: Create one location reference sheet for this single place: a establishing wide view plus 2-3 smaller angle studies of the same place, no people

inputImages.path: CHANGE: absolute style reference path — omit the whole array if input/style/ is empty

spatialStaging: panel layout: one large establishing view on the left, 2-3 smaller angle studies stacked on the right, thin neutral gutters between panels, no borders drawn as decoration

scene.place: CHANGE: paste locations[].nameAr + the full English visualDefinition — architecture type, scale, layout
scene.timeOfDay: CHANGE: the location's default light (pages may shift this, the geometry may not)
scene.atmosphere: CHANGE: mood + weather + air of this place
scene.lighting: CHANGE: key light direction, color temperature, shadow softness for the default hour
scene.foreground: CHANGE: fixed near elements that belong to this place permanently
scene.midground: CHANGE: the main stage where story action will happen
scene.background: CHANGE: far layer — skyline, horizon, far walls, depth cues
propsInFrame: CHANGE: every FIXED landmark of this place with color + material (a tree, a shop sign, a fountain, a striped rug). These must reappear on every page set here.
scene.backdropDetails: CHANGE: 3-6 concrete sensory details that make this place recognizable at a glance

style.medium: CHANGE: paste from themes/catalog.json for brief.themeId — identical to every page prompt
style.finish: CHANGE: paste from catalog for the same themeId

composition.viewpoint: eye-level establishing plus one high and one low study
composition.focalHierarchy: architecture and fixed landmarks first — this sheet exists to lock geometry, not mood

palette: CHANGE: this location's locked palette — pages may re-light it but not repaint it
constraints: one place only — never combine two locations on one sheet
absolutely no people, no characters, no animals
show the same place from every angle panel — same architecture, same landmarks, same materials
fixed landmarks must be clearly readable so pages can reuse them
landscape sheet (wider than tall) — same orientation as the book pages
empty stage: leave room where characters will later stand
avoid: a different building or layout between panels
compiledPrompt: CHANGE: single final prompt string for $imagegen describing this one empty place as a multi-angle reference sheet
